manifest.name: dsh-mathtype
manifest.description: MathType OLE equations for DeepSeek Harness: convert LaTeX placeholders in a Word document into real MathType objects (Equation.DSMT4) through the MathType SDK, preserving equation numbers, SEQ fields, bookmarks and cross-references.
manifest.author: DIPPER12138

bundle.text:
# dsh-mathtype bundle patch.
#
# Mounts the MathType skill registrar into the profile's layer stack. On load it
# reads skills/mathtype/SKILL.md out of this package and registers it into
# ctx.skills, so the `mathtype` skill appears in the catalog with no manual
# skill-root setup.
#
# Requires the `skills` service, which dsh-base mounts in every standard profile
# (row id `skill` -> @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill). `inject` makes the loader hand the
# service to the plugin; without it ctx.skills is undefined and the plugin only
# warns instead of registering anything.

- insert:
    - id: mathtype-skills
      name: 'dsh-mathtype/startup'
      inject: [skills]

readme.text:
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that converts LaTeX placeholders in a Word `.docx`
into **real MathType OLE objects** — `ProgID="Equation.DSMT4"`, a CFB container
holding an `Equation Native` stream — through the MathType SDK. The equations
double-click into MathType like any hand-authored one. They are not Word's
built-in OMML equations and not pictures.

*Left: the `\[ ... \]` LaTeX as written in the `.docx`. Right: what Word holds
after the run — real `Equation.DSMT4` objects, rendered here by Word itself.
The examples are textbook identities, chosen to show the format change rather
than any one manuscript's content.*

Because the document is edited in place through Word's own automation model,
existing equation numbers, `SEQ` fields, bookmarks, `REF` cross-references,
figures, tables and styles are never rebuilt.

One model-invocable skill, `mathtype`, registered into `ctx.skills` when the
plugin mounts:

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `mt_env.py` | Discovers MathType, `MT6.dll`, Word and Python deps; smoke-tests the SDK. |
| `mt_sdk.py` | `MT6.dll` wrapper: connect, `set_latex`, `get_text`, close. |
| `mt_prefs.py` | Equation size via the MathType registry block, restored afterwards. |
| `word_session.py` | Word session that survives RPC crashes and late-binding failures. |
| `convert_docx.py` | The conversion. `--dry-run`, `--overrides`, `--report`. |
| `verify_docx.py` | Structural proof: ProgID, CFB, `Equation Native`, rels, ShapeID, bookmarks, fields. |
| `render_check.py` | Export PDF, render page and per-equation QA sheets. |
| `make_fixture.py` | Build a 6-equation test document with real `SEQ` fields. |

No JavaScript dependencies: the registrar uses only `node:fs`, `node:path` and
`node:url`, so the package installs offline.

| Component | Requirement |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 10/11. COM and OLE have no macOS or Linux equivalent. |
| MathType | MathType 7 desktop, **full install** — the fonts-only package has no `System\<arch>\MT6.dll`. |
| Word | Desktop Word 2016/2019/2021/365. Not a viewer, not LibreOffice. |
| Python | 3.10+, bitness matching `MT6.dll` (64-bit Python ↔ `System\64\MT6.dll`). |
| Python packages | `pywin32`, `lxml`. Optional: `pymupdf` + `Pillow` for the render check. |

```bash
python -m pip install pywin32 lxml
python -m pip install pymupdf Pillow     # optional, render check only
```

Nothing is hard-coded: the MathType directory, SDK DLL and preference files are
resolved from the registry at run time, so a non-default install location works.
```bash

readme.section: from GitHub — use the profile you actually run (`desktop` or `web`)
readme.text: dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:DIPPER12138/dsh-mathtype

readme.section: or from a local checkout, for development
readme.text:
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/dsh-mathtype
```

Restart `dsh` afterwards. The `mathtype` skill then appears in the skill catalog.

If you previously copied this skill into `~/.dsh/skills/mathtype` by hand, delete
that copy — otherwise the same skill is registered twice.

The plugin cannot install MathType, Word or Python for you, and it cannot install
Python packages. Check the environment before converting anything:

```bash
python <skill-dir>/scripts/mt_env.py
```

It reports the resolved MathType directory and DLL, the Word version, dependency
status and a live `MTAPIConnect` result, and exits `0` only when the machine is
ready. On a new machine, prove the whole chain with the bundled fixture first
(about two minutes):

```bash
python scripts/make_fixture.py -o fixture.docx -f
python scripts/convert_docx.py fixture.docx -o fixture-out.docx --size 10.5
python scripts/verify_docx.py fixture.docx fixture-out.docx --expect 6
```
```bash

readme.section: what would be converted? (reads the .docx package only — no Word, no COM)
readme.text: python scripts/convert_docx.py manuscript.docx -o manuscript-MathType.docx --dry-run

python scripts/convert_docx.py manuscript.docx -o manuscript-MathType.docx \
        --size 10.5 --report conversion.json

readme.section: prove the objects are real MathType equations
readme.text: python scripts/verify_docx.py manuscript.docx manuscript-MathType.docx --expect 54

readme.section: optional: PDF export plus page/equation QA sheets
readme.text:
python scripts/render_check.py manuscript-MathType.docx --outdir qa
```

Recognised placeholders, one per paragraph:

| Source | Result |
|---|---|
| `\[a=b\tag{7}\]` | centred MathType object, number `(7)` right-aligned |
| `\[a=b\tag{2a}\]` | number `(2a)`; sub-lettering survives |
| `\[a=b\]` | centred object, no number |
| `$a=b$` | inline object |

readme.section: optional: PDF export plus page/equation QA sheets
readme.text:
Numbers inside `\tag{...}` are never regenerated: an existing `SEQ` field,
bookmark or literal `2a` is kept verbatim, so every `REF` still resolves.

`--size` sets the equation size (accepts `10.5` or `"10.5 pt"`); the previous
MathType setting is restored afterwards. `--align none` leaves paragraph layout
untouched. `--overrides fixes.json` replaces individual equations by label.

- Windows only.
- It converts existing LaTeX placeholders; it does not author or validate
  mathematics.
- It does not convert MathType back to LaTeX in batch (the SDK wrapper exposes
  `get_text()` for single equations).
- It does not produce Word OMML — that is the other direction.
- Requires the real MathType installation; the SDK DLL is never redistributed
  with this plugin.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-mathtype
```
